key_insight: A versatile two-layer model (VTLM) compresses 3D microchannel heat-sink conjugate heat transfer into two coupled 2D fields while preserving in-plane geometry and improving agreement with full 3D predictions.
engineering_relevance: VTLM offers a faster reduced-order tool for screening microchannel heat-sink designs and operating conditions without explicitly resolving the channel-height direction.
method: Couples two 2D fields to represent fluid and fin regions in place of a full 3D model.
Uses hydraulic and thermal closure relations to capture wall friction and interlayer heat transfer.
Derives closures from representative channel geometry, flow development, and fin configuration.
evidence_signal: The model was benchmarked against 3D reference simulations over broad ranges of channel aspect ratios, operating conditions, and both uniform and nonuniform fin arrangements, and it outperformed existing two-layer models overall.
watch_item: Accuracy depends strongly on flow-development condition and channel aspect ratio, so the proposed screening guideline should be applied cautiously outside the examined straight-channel and expansion-contraction cases.
paper_title: Versatile two-layer model for thermohydraulic prediction of microchannel heat sinks
